correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the orbit in RESULT.md lines 47–111 directly from the norming functional: its real center is δH, real phase radius C, and imaginary signed radius S. Compactness handles the zero-coordinate cases, and p=2 has S identically zero. The derivative of |S| on (0,1) has the stated numerator with constant sign factor sgn(p−2); differentiating that numerator gives a strictly one-signed derivative, since 2t^p−(p−2)−pt² has the sign of 2−p there. The endpoint signs and this strict derivative give a unique nondegenerate maximum up to reciprocal symmetry. The top witnesses have real parts ±δH(τ_p), so for nonzero split their missing midpoint proves strict axial loss and nonconvexity. Solving the real-part constraint gives the stated scalar objective; choosing t close to 1 but not equal proves positivity. The squared split is a smooth perturbation near the strict maximum; stationarity gives O_p(δ²) displacement, and the unperturbed deficit away from those neighborhoods excludes all other maximizers. Taylor expansion gives the quadratic coefficient with O_p(δ⁴) remainder. For the large-split limit, r=H/C vanishes only at 1 and diverges in magnitude at the two ends. It is locally invertible with derivative −p/2. In the feasible coordinate y=|δ|r, uniformly on [−1,1] the imaginary radius is |p−2||y|/(p|δ|)+O_p(|δ|^(−2)); multiplying by √(1−y²) and maximizing gives the claimed factor 1/2. At p=4 the squared objective is u(1−(1+4δ²)u)/(1+u)²; its derivative has numerator 1−(3+8δ²)u and changes sign at an interior feasible point. Its value, both modulus ratios and their phase conditions agree with the finding, also at δ=0. Read VERIFICATION.md and CHECK.py as finite diagnostics, not as proofs or certifications. The asymptotics are fixed-p and the large-split rate is for the axis height rather than its gap.
